parsed.stack: Ray-Ban Display HTML/CSS/JS caption surface + Neural Band, paired iOS/Android companion running on-device streaming ASR and on-device translation of flagged menu terms. Cloud ASR fallback (~$0.0025/min) for older/mid-range phones and high-noise rooms where the on-device model drops out. Menu glossary stored locally per venue. Freemium subscription.
milestones: Week 1-2: low-latency caption rendering on the Display at glanceable line lengths; latency budget under 600ms or it is useless mid-order.
Week 3-5: on-device streaming ASR in a loud dining room, with the cloud fallback and a hard monthly cap on fallback minutes per user.
Week 6-7: menu glossary - the wearer flags two unfamiliar terms per shift and they surface inline, which is the whole differentiator versus generic captions.
Week 8-9: shift-shaped UX: on for a table order, off otherwise, because always-on is both a battery and a privacy problem.
Week 10-11: freemium gate, pilot with two restaurants whose staff already own the hardware.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That live captioning is genuinely free - a 6-hour shift is ~360 minutes of continuous ASR, 20 shifts a month is 7,200 minutes, so every 25% of those minutes that fall back to cloud ASR costs ~$4.50 per active user per month, and at a 3% freemium conversion the ~100 free actives behind each payer make gross margin sharply negative.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: Run on-device streaming ASR on a mid-range Android in an actual busy dining room for one full shift and log the exact fraction of minutes where it degrades, drops out, or drains the battery below usable - one evening, no glasses required.
